wedgwood_librarian.text: The Wedgwood Institute, built in Josiah Wedgwood's memory in the 1860s. A library and a school of art and science, for working people.
Wedgwood lost the use of his leg to smallpox as a boy, so he couldn't work the potter's wheel well. He turned to experiments instead, and changed the whole industry.
He had his leg amputated in the end, in 1768, without anaesthetic. Then went straight back to work. Tough lot, potters.

darwin_student.text: Did you know Charles Darwin's mum was a Wedgwood? And then he married his cousin Emma Wedgwood. Wedgwood money paid for a lot of his science.
Josiah Wedgwood also made a medallion against slavery: a kneeling man in chains and the words Am I Not a Man and a Brother? Thousands were given away.
